description.narrative: The Government of Mongolia (GoM) has requested assistance from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to support a set of complementary medium-term structural reforms addressing climate change as its core objective. The proposed Accelerating Climate Investment Support Program will support Mongolia to strengthen the policy, planning and financing direction of GoM to accelerate investments in adaptation and mitigation priorities identified in its National Adaptation Plan (NAP) and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. The program will contribute to Mongolia's NDC Action Plan and will build on ADB supported investments in climate action. It is aligned with the ADB's Strategy 2030 and will support the implementation of operational priority 3 on tackling climate change, building climate and disaster resilience, and enhancing environmental sustainability. It will also support strategic priority 3 of ADB's Country Partnership Strategy (CPS) for Mongolia on resilience for sustainable, green, and climate-conscious development, and contribute to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 on taking urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts. It is also anchored in ADB's Climate Change Operational Framework, 2017-2030, which defines how ADB can facilitate a shift onto a development path that is climate-resilient and low in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, in line with the Paris Agreement, the Sustainable Development Goals, and the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction.

1.2. 2.1. The Financial Stability Council (consisting of MOF, BOM, FRC, and the Deposit Insurance Corporation of Mongolia) approved the National Sustainable Finance Roadmap of Mongolia to enhance financial flows for sustainable investments and increase the banks' and NBFIs' share of green loans and implemented key actions under the road map including the following: (i) FRC approving the regulation on the registration and issuance of green bonds in line with internationally recognized Green Bond Principles. (ii) BOM approving on a pilot basis the SDG Finance Taxonomy for enhancing investment opportunities in adaptation and mitigation that benefit women and climate-vulnerable groups.c, d (iii) MOF developing a framework for SDG bonds and obtaining a Second Party Opinion from S&P Global Ratings of its alignment with the ICMA Principles. (iv) BOM introducing preferential terms on green loan swaps. (v) BOM and FRC issuing ESG Reporting Guidelines for banks and NBFIs. (vi) BOM reporting green loan statistics on its website and initiating the collection of sex-disaggregated data of green loans from banks for disclosure.

3.1. To incentivize public and private sector investment in renewable energy, (i) Parliament approved the New Recovery Policy on Energy Recovery to enhance electricity and heat supply reliability, achieve financial sustainability, and increase the share of clean energy; and (ii) ERC issued a tariff increase on electricity and heating for non-household consumers.

3.2. Parliament approved the Resolution on Food Security with an action plan to promote measures on crop insurance, standards, green technology, and economic instruments to strengthen climate-risk management in crop, livestock, and food processing systems.

3.3. Parliament approved the Law on Safeguarding Negative Impacts and Pressing Challenges of Climate Change on Traditional Nomadic Herding to strengthen the capacity of herder cooperatives to manage climate risks.

To operationalize public and private investment in low-carbon and climate-resilient agriculture, (i) MOFALI will implement green lending under the New Cooperatives Program to enable herder cooperatives to access finance for investment in climate-resilient practices; (ii) MASM will approve and publish climate-related agriculture standards on crop, livestock, or food processing systems developed by MOFALI and build the capacity of certification agencies, agriculture enterprises, and herder cooperatives, including enterprises owned or led by women to apply the standards; and (iii) MOF will implement a tax policy to promote low-carbon and sustainable agriculture practices. Base year: 2024 Target date: 2026-09-15 Target value: 100 MW
Action 3: Long-Term Strategy and Diversification
To promote a low carbon and climate resilient economy the: (i) Government will develop Long-term Climate Strategies (LTS) to strengthen and guide its submission of updated NDCs to UNFCCC. (ii) Government will develop a Climate-Smart Mining Strategy focused on positioning Mongolia in the global clean energy technology supply chain to diversify its economy from coal dependence. Base year: 2024 Target date: 2026-09-15 Target value: 100 MW
Action 1: 1.4. To incentivize public and private sector investment in renewable energy, (i) Parliament approved the New Recovery Policy on Energy Recovery to enhance electricity and heat supply reliability, achieve financial sustainability, and increase the share of clean energy; and (ii) ERC issued a tariff increase on electricity and heating for non-household consumers. Base year: 2024 Target date: 2024-09-15 Target value: 100
